body: Saturday, August 22 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto

Macro Stance: The Fed is in a hawkish hold with an active tightening bias. July FOMC minutes released this week revealed officials saw a "need for rate hike if inflation doesn't cool," with a September hike explicitly still on the table. Fiscal remains expansive and deficit concerns are acute — the 30-year yield topped 5.31% (highest in 19 years) on Aug 17 and El-Erian called the 5.27% level a "structural shift." The 10Y at 4.74 (+6 bps vs 4W) and 2Y at 4.24% (prior close, −9 bps) produce a +50 bps curve — positively sloped but still flat by historical standards, and 14 bps steeper than four weeks ago as the long end carries term premium while the front end edges lower. Treasury Secretary Bessent acted to "break bond market fever" via buyback operations, and crypto/gold markets explicitly rallied on the buyback announcement, confirming this was read as quasi-liquidity injection.

New / Most Important: This is the week the US bond market forced the administration's hand — again. Bessent's emergency buyback operation (reported Aug 19-20) was a direct response to alarming long-end yields. The FOMC minutes (Aug 19-20) simultaneously revealed a hawkish contingency that markets had not fully priced. This creates a structurally novel tension: the Treasury is injecting liquidity at the long end to suppress term premium while the Fed is signaling it may tighten further at the short end. This is effectively a policy conflict — fiscal dominance in real time. The equity market is shrugging it off (S&P 7674, ↑3.5%) because the buybacks are functionally acting like sterilized QE, improving collateral conditions and freeing dealer balance sheets. Gold at 4624 (↑13.7%) and Bitcoin at 77261 (↑21.7%) are the honest markets here — they are pricing the debasement channel, not the rate channel. Watch for this Treasury buyback mechanism to become a recurring feature — it's the new "not-QE."

Playbook ✓: Equities grinding higher on AI/mega-cap leadership (Nasdaq ↑4.2% vs Russell ↑3.0%, narrow market confirmed). VIX crushed to 15.1 in COMPLACENCY regime despite bond stress — classic late-cycle risk appetite. New Trump tariffs on Canada announced, keeping trade uncertainty alive.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The massive divergence is that the bond market is screaming fiscal unsustainability while equities remain near highs. Historically a curve steepening on rising long-end yields (not Fed cuts) — even to a still-flat +50 bps — is a warning of sovereign credit deterioration, not a risk-on signal. Gold up 13.7% in four weeks while China's July bank loans posted a record contraction confirms this is not healthy reflation — it's defensive positioning masquerading as momentum. The fact that Treasury had to intervene with buybacks to calm the 30-year market is a fiscal dominance signal that structurally changes the playbook: the Fed's rate decisions are becoming secondary to Treasury's debt management operations as the primary driver of financial conditions.

Macro Stance: ECB in a data-dependent hold. Kazāks stated the bank is "well placed to act if needed to get inflation to 2%," suggesting optionality in both directions. The euro gained on hawkish ECB outlook this week, even against a firmer dollar.

New / Most Important: Goldman Sachs highlighted European stocks "defying global shocks with strong earnings growth" — a relative outperformance story that is gaining institutional traction. ECB research on how bank funding structures affect rate transmission suggests they're preparing the intellectual groundwork for more unconventional tools. Lagarde's warning that Europe "can't afford to miss the AI revolution" signals fiscal willingness to support tech capex.

Playbook ✓: European equities benefiting from relative valuation discount and dollar weakness trend. Earnings delivery beating low expectations.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Europe is becoming a beneficiary of US bond stress — capital fleeing US duration is finding European equities as a relative safe haven with better fiscal metrics. This is a reversal of the 2022-24 pattern where Europe was the source of outflows. If US Treasury buybacks redirect capital toward Asia (as Nation Thailand reported), Europe may also catch a bid from the rebalancing flow.

Macro Stance: Rates are on hold and the burden has shifted to the budget. China kept loan prime rates steady for a 15th month (Reuters, [Aug 19]), the 1-year at 3.0% and the 5-year at 3.5% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 19]), while expanding consumer and small-business loan subsidies (The Asian Banker, [Aug 21]); liquidity runs through the overnight window, with 7-day reverse repos at zero for seven straight sessions (BigGo Finance, [Aug 19]). The yuan surged to 6.72 per dollar, a 42-month high (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]), even as the PBOC fixed at 6.7808, weaker than the previous fix (CryptoRank, [Aug 20]) and well above the 6.7262 Reuters estimate (investingLive, [Aug 20]), a deliberate brake after its move to slow yuan gains (Bloomberg, [Aug 19]). Prices leave room to ease: July CPI rose 0.5% and PPI growth slowed to 3.5%, both missing expectations (BigGo Finance, [Aug 8]).

PMIs & Activity: July's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.2 and non-manufacturing to 49.0 (FXStreet, [Jul 31]); the private factory gauge eased to 50.9 (Fibre2Fashion, [Aug 3]) and private services growth was the slowest since September 2024 (Reuters, [Aug 4]). The hard data confirmed the slide: industrial output grew 4.5% y/y and retail sales just 0.6% (Reuters, [Aug 17]), and fixed-asset investment fell 6.7% in the first seven months (Xinhua, [Aug 17]); services spending is at least outpacing goods (Caixin Global, [Aug 21]). Exports remain the engine, jumping almost a quarter in July (Financial Times, [Aug 6]). The August flash PMIs abroad went the other way: euro-zone activity grew at the fastest pace since November (Reuters, [Aug 21]), the US composite improved to 56 (Kitco, [Aug 21]) and Japan's manufacturing PMI jumped to 55.1 on chip and AI orders (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]), a cycle China supplies but does not share.

Credit Impulse: July new bank loans posted a record contraction as credit demand faltered (Reuters, [Aug 14]), only the second contraction this year (The Standard (HK), [Aug 14]), yet Bloomberg reports credit growth exceeded forecasts despite the rare loan slump ([Aug 14]). Reconciled: headline financing, which includes bond issuance, beat; bank lending to households and firms shrank, leaving cumulative yuan loans up 10.38 trillion yuan in January–July (Xinhua, [Aug 14]). The expanded subsidised-loan programme (Caixin Global, [Aug 21]) targets that gap by cutting the effective cost of SME and consumer borrowing without touching the LPR; whether it revives demand is the August credit print's question.

Property: July new home prices were stagnant as demand stayed weak (Reuters, [Aug 17]) and first-tier prices were flat, ending a four-month rebound (South China Morning Post, [Aug 17]); the 70-city index fell 3.2% y/y, the smallest drop in five months, while property investment slumped nearly 20% (BigGo Finance, [Aug 17]). A flood of discounted auction homes is deepening the slump (Asia Times, [Aug 21]). Policy is granular: Shanghai started a new round of easing (Bloomberg, [Aug 19]) and is lowering second-home down payments (South China Morning Post, [Aug 20]), and housing provident fund rules are being reshaped (China.org.cn, [Aug 21]). A court accepted Evergrande's liquidation a day after its founder's life sentence (South China Morning Post, [Aug 21]), with creditors still owed $300 billion (Fortune, [Aug 21]).

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: China plans new fiscal support policies amid the growth slowdown (Bloomberg, [Aug 21]) and new measures to boost domestic demand in the second half (Global Times, [Aug 21]), and unveiled steps to boost weak consumption (South China Morning Post, [Aug 21]) after pledging timely fiscal support (Reuters, [Aug 20]) and raising the SME interest-subsidy loan cap to 75 million yuan (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]). Revenue gives some room, with public budget revenue up 5.8% in the first seven months (China Daily, [Aug 21]). Trade is fragmenting: Beijing rejected a US tariff report as Mexico plans new China curbs (South China Morning Post, [Aug 21]), slammed EU foreign-subsidy rules and linked them to trade talks (POLITICO.eu, [Aug 21]), and struck a Swiss deal scrapping most levies (Bloomberg, [Aug 20]); India is leaving the door ajar for Chinese investors.

Markets & Flows: The Hang Seng rose 1.21% to reclaim 26,000 (Moomoo, [Aug 21]), its fifth straight gain (Dimsum Daily, [Aug 21]), and A-shares closed higher as precious metals led (BigGo Finance, [Aug 21]) while investors await fiscal support (The Economic Times, [Aug 21]). Flows are mixed: mainland capital pulled a net HK$10.4 billion from Hong Kong stocks (BigGo Finance, [Aug 20]), materials names are emerging as market leaders (Bloomberg, [Aug 20]), and China trimmed US Treasury holdings as the global reserve shift gathers pace (Firstpost, [Aug 18]).

New / Most Important: Fiscal policy is now explicitly the lead instrument. New support policies, a second-half demand package and an expanded subsidised-loan scheme follow an LPR hold, so the mix is budget-funded and aimed at consumers and SMEs, with no rate cut and a yuan held back by weaker fixings. Evergrande's liquidation closes the legal chapter of the bust, not the economic one.

Playbook ✓: Rates on hold, targeted fiscal support, city-level property easing and a managed yuan are on script.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The August flash PMIs show the US and euro-area cycle accelerating without China, whose own July data missed and whose loans contracted. That gap decides transmission: iron ore rose only as China demand concerns met stimulus hopes (TradingView, [Aug 18]), so AUD, at a two-month high on US Treasury buybacks (Moomoo, [Aug 19]) rather than Chinese demand, is exposed if the fiscal package underwhelms. European industry feels the "China shock" (Axios, [Aug 21]), with a German state politician calling for EU tariffs on Chinese hybrids (Reuters, [Aug 21]), and Iranian oil offers to Chinese buyers fell as the US blockade bites (Reuters, [Aug 21]), raising China's import bill with WTI at 87.06.

Macro Stance: The BoJ is converging toward its first rate hike in 31 years with accelerating momentum. Japanese inflation picked up further this week, backing the case for tightening. Multiple sources — Mizuho, Bloomberg, FT — all confirmed rising inflation data and strengthening hike expectations. The yen strengthened against the dollar as rate hike bets solidified.

New / Most Important: This is the most consequential central bank story globally right now and it is structurally NEW in a generational sense. Japan has not hiked rates since the early 1990s; the prospect of normalization threatens to unwind the world's largest carry trade. The yen carry trade unwind fears are colliding with easing oil prices, creating a complex cross-asset dynamic. Takaichi's BoJ appointments in 2027 loom as a political constraint on the pace of hikes, but the market is front-running the near-term move. Morgan Stanley flagged the "weak yen matters to investors" — this is the flip side: if the yen strengthens sharply on a hike, Japanese institutional repatriation of foreign bond holdings (particularly US Treasuries) would compound the US long-end problem. This is the most dangerous feedback loop in global macro right now: BoJ hikes → yen strengthens → Japanese investors sell US Treasuries → US yields spike further → Treasury forced into more buybacks → dollar weakens → yen strengthens further. Japanese corporate bond issuers are already flagging rate hikes as a "hurdle," suggesting credit conditions will tighten domestically.

Playbook ✓: Inflation data supporting normalization narrative. Yen appreciation on hawkish repricing.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The political overlay (Takaichi's 2027 BoJ appointments) could cap the hiking cycle before it gets meaningful. The market may be pricing a more aggressive path than the BoJ can deliver given political constraints. But even a single hike could trigger the repatriation cascade described above.

Macro Stance: RBA maintaining a hawkish hold with explicit tightening bias. Deputy Governor Hauser warned of "higher rates if inflation risks crystallise." Governor's "blunt warning" — "We will do so" — regarding further hikes. Employment growth remains too strong for the RBA's comfort, though softer jobs data this week introduced some ambiguity.

New / Most Important: RBA sounded an alarm on states' debt binge — a rare fiscal warning from the central bank that echoes the US term premium story at a smaller scale. Softer jobs data slightly eased tightening bets but the overall hawkish rhetoric remains dominant.  |  Playbook ✓: AUD holding near highs on hawkish RBA and broad dollar weakness.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: The combination of state-level fiscal excess and potential RBA hikes creates a policy collision similar to the US but less severe. Negative equity risks flagged in housing remain a tail risk if they actually hike.

Macro Stance: The RPP is on hold, but the minutes released today show which members wanted a hike (Tysol.pl, [Aug 22]), the first documented push for tightening this cycle. PKO BP's economists counter that labour data will not sway the Council (wnp.pl, [Aug 20]), yet the data are strong: July enterprise wages rose 6.8% y/y with employment down 0.8% (Do Rzeczy, [Aug 20]), the average wage hit 9509 zł (CEO Magazyn, [Aug 20]), industrial output grew 5.1% y/y (PAP Biznes, [Aug 20]); construction stayed below the line (Parkiet, [Aug 20]) and Q3 forecasts point to a slowdown (Strefa Biznesu, [Aug 20]). On prices, PPI reaccelerated to 2.8% in July (CEO Magazyn, [Aug 20]); HICP was 3.1% (Do Rzeczy, [Aug 19]). Citi expects fuel measures extended at least through September (PAP Biznes, [Aug 17]), yet maximum fuel prices rise from Saturday (Portal Spożywczy, [Aug 21]) and refineries pushed another wave of wholesale increases (Super Biznes, [Aug 22]).

Markets: The week closed with gains and Dino as the star (Parkiet, [Aug 21]): up 5.5% with the WIG20 up 1% mid-session (Bankier.pl, [Aug 21]), more than 8% at the close (CrypS.pl, [Aug 21]), on close to 1.5 billion zł of turnover in Dino and KGHM (Bankier.pl, [Aug 21]). That reversed a three-day slide in which Parkiet saw indices drifting from bull-market peaks [Aug 19]. The card confirms the rotation: Dino 34.78 (+7.3% 1W, +20.8% 4W), PKO 113.96 (+2.6% 1W) and Pekao 258.8 (+10.7% 4W) carry the index, while KGHM 342.35 (-2.9% 1W, +12.8% 4W), PGE 10.19 (-5.6% 1W), LPP 20,800 (-4.7% 1W), Allegro 45.1 (-2.9% 1W) and CD Projekt 258.7 (-1.7% 1W, +14.4% 4W) lag; EPOL 44.42 is flat on the week (+8.6% 4W). The structural headline is S&P Dow Jones Indices upgrading Poland to developed-market status (Reuters, [Aug 21]). The zloty is at a two-month high against the dollar, with Comparic.pl asking whether another 5 groszy comes off [Aug 22]; the dollar fell to 3.68 (CEO Magazyn, [Aug 21]), and the card has USD/PLN 3.6918 (-1.2% 1W, -3.0% 4W), EUR/PLN 4.3146 (+0.1% 1W, -0.4% 4W). POLGBs have only a global catalyst: Parkiet calls it an SOS from the US bond market [Aug 22], the US 30-year is at 5.27% (BeInCrypto, [Aug 17]), US debt passed 40 trillion dollars (Bankier.pl, [Aug 20]).

Fiscal & Politics: Fitch affirmed Poland at A- with a negative outlook (PAP, [Aug 22]; Gov.pl, [Aug 21]). Domański called it very good news (PolsatNews.pl, [Aug 22]), but the agency attached a serious warning on deficit and rising debt (Portal Samorządowy, CEO Magazyn, [Aug 22]) and flagged pre-election risks (Parkiet, [Aug 22]). The draft is public: lower taxes for citizens, higher for giants and lump-sum payers (Bankier.pl, [Aug 22]), a rate rising from 19 to 22% from 2027 (Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 21]), CIT at 30% for the largest energy firms (Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 20]) under which Orlen, PGE, Enea and Tauron add close to 7 billion zł (Rzeczpospolita, [Aug 21]), and a new levy funding 4.8 billion zł of power-price compensation for energy-intensive industry (Gazeta Prawna, [Aug 21]). The veto risk is explicit: Gazeta Prawna reports Nawrocki may veto the package [Aug 21]. Tusk called an extra cabinet meeting on the budget (Polskie Radio 24, [Aug 21]) with the deficit past 141 billion zł after July (Bankier.pl, [Aug 17]).

Corporate & Sectors: KGHM followed its record half, nearly 5.6 billion zł of profit (Strefa Biznesu, [Aug 21]) and EBITDA up 89% y/y (Strefa Inwestorów, [Aug 21]), with expansion talk: WNP.PL reports it is quietly going after a second mine in Chile [Aug 22] and is eyeing a US listing (wnp.pl, [Aug 21]). Dino's Q2 was in line (Strefa Inwestorów, [Aug 21]): 400 million zł net and 3176 stores (StockWatch.pl, [Aug 21]), profitability slightly lower (Parkiet, [Aug 21]) and only a slow LFL recovery expected in H2 (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 21]); pb.pl's verdict was that the absence of disappointment was enough [Aug 21]. StockWatch.pl worked through what a 30% CIT means for Orlen dividends [Aug 21]; PGE and Ørsted finished all 111 Baltica 2 monopiles on schedule (Inwestycje.pl, [Aug 21]). CD Projekt is rising into its Gamescom showcase (INNPoland.pl, [Aug 21]) after the Edgerunners 2 date and trailer (CD PROJEKT RED IR, [Aug 21]). Banks: PKO BP got KNF approval for portfolio management (Bankier.pl, [Aug 21]), but Franknews says over 68 thousand repaid CHF contracts could be challenged [Aug 21] and BNP Paribas admits a 73.6% loss rate in CHF suits [Aug 22]; Poland has the third most expensive mortgages in the EU (Obserwator Gospodarczy, [Aug 22]) even with margins near multi-year lows (Bankier.pl, [Aug 20]).

Geopolitics & Security: Tarcza Wschód reached initial operational readiness in many sections after two years (Strefa Obrony, [Aug 21]), with Bundeswehr support (INNPoland.pl, [Aug 22]) and MON saying the border can be mined within 48 hours (Interia, [Aug 21]). The US deployed a spy plane to Poland (Firstpost, [Aug 21]), NATO ran unannounced exercises near Kaliningrad (UNN, [Aug 21]), Romania says Russian strikes increasingly spill into NATO (ABC News, [Aug 21]). Defence spending is to reach 5% of GDP by 2027 (TodayPress.tv, [Aug 21]).

New / Most Important: Two verdicts on Poland landed within a day: S&P Dow Jones promoted the market to developed status while Fitch kept the A- rating on a negative outlook with a warning on deficit and debt. The equity story is institutionally accepted but the sovereign is on probation, with the pre-election budget and a vetoable tax package as the test; minutes showing hike advocates on the RPP tilt the rate path up, not down.  |  Playbook ✓: Hold with a hawkish bias; banks and Dino are the earnings-backed longs, zloty strength is a dollar story to ride rather than chase, and POLGB duration stays light while US yields set the tone.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: Dino jumped more than 8% on results Parkiet calls weak with falling profitability, and the zloty sits at two-month highs under a negative rating outlook: positioning, not fundamentals, is driving both.

Macro Stance: Rupee edging higher to 95.70 as dollar weakness offsets crude oil pressure. India is uniquely positioned this week: opening to Chinese investment while benefiting from US Treasury buyback-driven capital redirection toward Asia.

New / Most Important: India "leaving the door ajar for China's investors" is the most important EM development this week. This pragmatic pivot — allowing Chinese capital while maintaining geopolitical alignment with the West — could make India the biggest beneficiary of the US-China decoupling if it can absorb both Western and Chinese capital simultaneously. Yahoo Finance flagged "investment opportunities in India" — institutional interest is building. The rupee's stability despite oil at 87 (normally a headwind for India) suggests improved current account dynamics or strong portfolio inflows.  |  Playbook ✓: Benefiting from dollar weakness and EM allocation flows.  |  ⚠️ Divergence: India accepting Chinese FDI breaks the decoupling consensus and could create friction with the US.

Narrative: Mega-cap tech keeps leading — Nasdaq ↑4.2% vs Russell ↑3.0% confirms narrow leadership — with the AI capex cycle visible in $177K advertised AI salaries and Nvidia's earnings looming as the next catalyst.

Reported: Keysight beat by $0.59 with revenue above estimates (Investing.com, [Aug 18]), and its shares rose after record third-quarter results (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 19]). Fabrinet beat on strong data-centre growth (Zacks Investment Research, [Aug 18]) but tumbled despite an upbeat Q1 outlook (Seeking Alpha, [Aug 18]). Ubiquiti beat by $0.25 with revenue above estimates (Investing.com, [Aug 21]).

EPS Upside Watch: Salesforce — rallying into earnings as Agentforce tops $1 billion (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 21]), an AI revenue line that answers the seat-license worry. CrowdStrike — Benchmark says it could beat Q2 expectations across the board (Stocktwits, [Aug 18]); the stock then sank 7% despite a Truist target raise (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 19]), resetting the bar.

⚡ Breaking Convention: A large fund selling Nvidia before earnings to buy Warner Bros. is a contrarian signal: if AI's value accrues to content owners rather than chipmakers at this stage of the cycle, the semiconductor premium is at risk — still a minority view, but the rotation is real.
Narrative: Communications benefits from mega-cap momentum and AI-driven engagement, and Warner Bros. as the chosen rotation target from Nvidia signals institutional interest in content and IP.

Reported: China's platforms disappointed. Baidu's revenue miss sank its shares as its CEO vowed to return Ernie to the AI frontier (Reuters, [Aug 18]); Kuaishou's earnings dropped by a third, hit by AI and creator costs (Bloomberg.com, [Aug 19]); NetEase fell as a Q2 earnings miss overshadowed stronger revenue (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 20]).

EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet — Google Cloud's backlog hit $514 billion in the same quarter capex guidance was raised to $205 billion (The Motley Fool, [Aug 16]): booked demand that converts into cloud revenue.

⚡ Breaking Convention: AI is a cost line before it is a revenue line: Baidu and Kuaishou show that platforms without compute to sell pay for AI out of margins, so the AI-adjacent bid should favour sellers of cloud capacity and owners of scarce content over pure ad platforms.

Narrative: A modestly steepening curve (+50 bps 10s-2s, still flat by historical standards) is only mildly positive for NIMs, and fiscal term premium drives the steepening — good for trading desks, a threat to loan books if long rates stay elevated.

Reported: Klarna dropped 19% after cutting its full-year guidance (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 18]) as German retail weakened (Reuters, [Aug 18]). Absa posted higher half-year profit as credit costs eased (Reuters, [Aug 17]). National Australia Bank's fiscal Q3 cash earnings rose, but its shares fell 4% (MarketScreener, [Aug 16]).

EPS Upside Watch: Canada's Big Six banks — head into Q3 earnings on four-quarter beat streaks (Investing.com Canada, [Aug 21]), though they face a tougher test after a stock selloff (Bloomberg.com, [Aug 21]). HSBC — RBC raised its price target as earnings forecasts climb (Proactive financial news, [Aug 17]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Treasury buyback operations are an under-discussed tailwind for primary dealers and bank Treasury holdings: banks holding long-duration Treasuries just got a put option from the government, softening the unrealized-loss problem that high long-end yields create.

Narrative: WTI at 87.06 (↓2.5% vs 4W) while oil stocks are "catching fire" per IBD: with China's July factory PMI at 49.2 and its bank loans contracting, the equity bid reads as a supply-shock story, not demand-led strength.

Reported: Santos beat first-half profit estimates and sees second-half output rising (Reuters, [Aug 18]). Ithaca Energy raised its 2026 dividend guidance after record North Sea production (Yahoo Finance UK, [Aug 19]). Energy Transfer raised its 2026 guidance (The Motley Fool, [Aug 16]).

EPS Upside Watch: ExxonMobil and Chevron — oil profits have more than doubled, and an escalating Iran war is the swing factor for both (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 17]), after oil majors reaped a $93 billion windfall from the war (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 16]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Oil stocks outperforming while crude drops is classic late-cycle behaviour: equities are pricing supply tightness the crude market has not, or riding the inflation-hedge bid alongside gold. Demand is not collapsing either — the US flash composite PMI improved to 56 in August — so the supply-shock premium looks real.

Narrative: The collapse of US-Canada trade talks and new Trump tariffs on Canada add uncertainty for cross-border industrials, while Hyundai's Georgia Metaplant expansion to 800K units is a reshoring tailwind.

Reported: Deere rallied 7% after quarterly profit climbed and it raised its full-year forecast (TIKR.com, [Aug 21]), with data-centre construction bolstering its sales guidance (Manufacturing Dive, [Aug 21]). Nordson beat on broad organic growth (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 21]). Curtiss-Wright raised guidance again (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 15]).

EPS Upside Watch: Honeywell — revenue acceleration and earnings growth prospects at a reasonable valuation (Seeking Alpha, [Aug 21]). Expeditors — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 18]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: AI is lifting industrial valuations toward tech's (Barron's, [Aug 20]), and Deere's data-centre construction demand shows how far the capex reaches: these names now trade as growth stocks, so they would take tech-style losses if AI capex wobbles, while tariff-exposed cross-border names trade on Canada.
Narrative: Tariff refunds are reaching retailers' books — returned to shoppers or reinvested — while higher-for-longer rates pressure housing-sensitive discretionary names.

Reported: Ross Stores surged 9% after beating estimates and lifting guidance (TIKR.com, [Aug 21]). Home Depot beat and reaffirmed guidance despite "frozen housing market conditions" (CNBC, [Aug 18]), and the stock rose (Barron's, [Aug 18]). Advance Auto Parts plunged 21% as a revenue miss overshadowed its earnings beat (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 20]).

EPS Upside Watch: H&M — analysts raised their forecasts ahead of the results (Il Sole 24 ORE, [Aug 18]). Amazon — Morgan Stanley raised its target to $500, seeing AWS revenue reaching $1 trillion in the AI era (Moomoo, [Aug 18]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Off-price split on execution, not demand: Ross jumped after raising its full-year profit guidance (Reuters, [Aug 21]) while a "self-inflicted" slowdown clouded TJX's beat (Reuters, [Aug 19]). The weak consumer shows up first in footwear — JD Sports cut its profit outlook as US sales dropped (Reuters, [Aug 20]).
Narrative: Defensive staples underperform in a risk-on tape, and rising yields make their dividend yields less attractive on a relative basis.

Reported: Walmart beat and raised guidance, yet the stock crashed (24/7 Wall St., [Aug 21]), sliding 9% as a sales growth slowdown tests consumer resilience (Reuters, [Aug 21]). BJ's Wholesale popped on an earnings beat and raised outlook (Schaeffer's Investment Research, [Aug 21]). Estée Lauder jumped 11.8% on a sales beat (StockStory, [Aug 19]).

EPS Upside Watch: Target — hit a 52-week high as analysts lifted price targets after its beat (BigGo Finance, [Aug 21]), with almost $1 billion in tariff refunds it plans to use to lower prices (Modern Retail, [Aug 19]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Walmart's slowdown could portend trouble for packaged food brands (FoodNavigator.com, [Aug 21]): when the largest grocer reinvests $2.9 billion of tariff refunds in lower prices (CBS News, [Aug 20]), the retailer buys share and the brands fund the price war — staples' defensive label hides that squeeze.
Narrative: Healthcare's defensive characteristics are less valued with the VIX at 15.1 in complacency mode, so the sector trades on single-stock results rather than as a haven.

Reported: CSL rallied 18% on its earnings beat (Livewire Markets, [Aug 17]) as cost cuts beat target and FY27 guidance cleared the bar (Kalkine, [Aug 20]). Basilea lifted guidance after strong half-year results (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 21]). Hengrui saw profit growth squeezed by China's bulk-buying programs (Reuters, [Aug 19]).
EPS Upside Watch: Iovance Biotherapeutics — UBS raised its price target on a revenue beat (Investing.com, [Aug 20]). GeneDx — earnings estimates are rising (Yahoo Finance, [Aug 19]).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Big Pharma's strong Q2 masks a looming cliff (BigGo Finance, [Aug 21]) just as Chinese drugmakers move up the value chain — innovative drugs topped 60% of Hengrui's H1 revenue (BigGo Finance, [Aug 19]). The pipeline gap, not the quarter, is the sector's earnings risk.
Narrative: Copper ↑4.1% on AI data-centre and grid capex and gold ↑13.7% at 4,624; miners rose even as the Dow fell 700 points on Aug 20, and steel benefits from the Canada trade collapse.

Reported: BHP's profit topped estimates as copper powered growth, with its highest dividend in 4 years (Reuters, [Aug 17]), copper now its growth "engine" amid the data centre boom (This is Money, [Aug 18]).
